newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Serbs accused of blocking court orders.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serbs accused of blocking court orders.

text.p: Bosnian Serb police have refused to enforce court rulings seeking to overturn wartime "ethnic cleansing" of Moslem and Croat families, international human rights monitors reported on Tuesday.
A local court in the Serb-controlled town of Banja Luka has ordered 38 families to be reinstated in their flats after they were expelled during the 1992-95 war.

But Banja Luka police have failed to uphold the court orders in violation of the Serb entity's laws and the Dayton peace agreement, said a statement issued by monitors from the United Nations and other international agencies.

The Moslem and Croat families who were expelled had decided to stay in the Banja Luka region rather than flee to other areas in Bosnia and had paid contributions to Serb wartime organisations, the statement said.
Human rights workers said the failure of local police to execute court orders was "deplorable" and said the police had failed to meet a June 7 deadline set by the country's peacetime ombudsperson.

Serb forces backed by the Yugoslav army carried out brutal expulsions of Moslems and Croats early in the war in an "ethnic cleansing" campaign. Notorious detention camps were set up in the Banja Luka region, where hundreds of thousands of people were evicted.

The Dayton peace treaty guarantees Bosnians the right to return to their pre-war homes but the refusal by Serb police to obey their own courts dast "grave doubts" about prospects for any return of refugees, it said.
"We want to see compliance with their own court judgements," Michael Maclay, spokesman for the internatonal High Representative to Bosnia, told reporters.
The deputy High Representative, Michael Steiner, planned to raise the issue in talks with Biljana Plavsic, the president of Bosnia's Serb republic.
Western diplomats see Plavsic as more willing to abide by the Dayton treaty than her political rival, Momcilo Krajisnik, a member of the country's collective presidency.

Plavsic recently spoke out in support of an independent judiciary in remarks clearly aimed at Krajisnik and indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic, who rule Serb territory through a large police force.
Krajisnik and the rest of the Serb leadership have sought to isolate Plavsic after she called for an investigation into war profiteering and corruption a few months ago.
